reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported (orders 260 and 263 with amounts 8294 and 8982). Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches what W2 reported: orders 260 (8294) and 263 (8982). Next I need the list of customers so I can get each net balance, so I'll call list_orders.
The refunds table matches what W2 reported, so I can proceed. The customers in the orders are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Refunds match W2's report. Acme's net balance is 29089. Next, get birch's net balance.
Refunds match W2's report. So far acme is 29089 and birch is 62075. Cobalt is the third customer in the orders list, so I need its net balance next.
Refunds match W2's report, and all three net balances are in hand: acme 29089, birch 62075, cobalt 50341. Recording one payout per customer, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt remain, and both net balances are already in hand, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 50341 was already fetched and the refunds matched W2's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts recorded successfully. The refunds matched W2's report, and each net balance agrees with its orders minus refunds (acme 46365 - 17276 = 29089, birch 62075, cobalt 50341).
